## Equal cosines · The unit circle {#fgt2-cosine-equality .trig-lesson .application-lesson}

Cosine is the **horizontal coordinate** on the unit circle.

```{=html}
<div data-periodic="cosine-equality" class="periodic-demo"></div>
```

<p class="booklet-cue">Support for Example 2.6(c) · Use both angle relationships when solving.</p>

::: notes

This is supporting instruction, not a new booklet question. Begin with Same angle: the two points coincide, so the cosine values agree. Select Full turn to show θ2=θ1+2π. The purple angle arrow loops once more before reaching the same direction; its turns are spaced apart so that the extra revolution is visible. At the initial setting, θ1=π/3 and θ2=7π/3 have the same cosine, 1/2. The angles are different but their terminal points coincide. Switch to Reflected angle: reflection in the horizontal axis gives the same horizontal coordinate. The relevant quadrant pairs are I and IV, or II and III. Move the angle slider through both pairs, including negative cosine values; a shared reference angle alone does not guarantee the same cosine sign. At angles on the horizontal axis, the two reflected points coincide.

The slider keeps θ1 in the first positive revolution. Full turn places θ2 one revolution beyond θ1; Same angle and Reflected angle keep θ2 in the first revolution. The reflected angle is 2π−θ1, equivalent to −θ1 modulo a full turn. Full turns give the complete rule: cos θ1=cos θ2 if and only if θ2=θ1+2mπ or θ2=−θ1+2mπ, for an integer m. The two displayed alternatives include all solutions; they may describe the same point on an axis. Reset restores θ1=π/3 and Same angle. Slider increments are π/24; displayed cosine readings are rounded to three decimals.

For Example 2.6(c), identify θ1=πt/24 and θ2=π(t−6)/24=θ1−π/4. Use the two branches in OneNote on the next slide. The same-angle branch would require −π/4=2mπ, impossible for integer m. The reflected branch gives θ1−π/4=−θ1+2mπ, so t=3+24m. At t=3, θ2=−π/8 (equivalent to 15π/8); at t=27, the angles are 9π/8 and 7π/8, in quadrants III and II. The first pair has positive cosine and the second negative cosine. Since A(t)=21−18 cos θ1, the positive cosine pair gives the lower equal height. Allow about 4 minutes.

:::
